title: Concept Notes: Exploring Real Numbers, Irrationals & Surds
objectives: Classify numbers across natural, whole, integer, rational, irrational, and real number sets
Convert non-terminating recurring decimals into rational p/q fractions
Understand the geometric meaning of real numbers on the continuous number line

blocks.heading: The Real Number System (R)
blocks.content:
A number is **rational (Q)** if it can be written as $p/q$, where $p, q \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $q \ne 0$.
A number is **irrational** if it CANNOT be written in $p/q$ form.
Together, all rational and irrational numbers form the collection of **real numbers (R)**. Every real number is represented by a unique point on the number line, and conversely, every point on the number line represents a unique real number.

blocks.heading: Decimal Expansions & The Rationality Test
blocks.content:
• **Terminating:** e.g., $1/2 = 0.5$, $7/8 = 0.875$. Rational!
• **Non-terminating Recurring:** e.g., $1/3 = 0.333\dots = 0.\overline{3}$, $1/7 = 0.\overline{142857}$. Rational!
• **Non-terminating Non-recurring:** e.g., $\sqrt{2} = 1.41421356\dots$, $\pi = 3.14159265\dots$. Strictly **IRRATIONAL**!

blocks.heading: Properties of Operations on Real Numbers
blocks.content:
1. The sum or difference of a rational number and an irrational number is always **irrational**.
2. The product or quotient of a non-zero rational number with an irrational number is always **irrational**.
3. The sum, difference, product, or quotient of two irrationals may be rational or irrational (e.g. $\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2} = 2$ is rational, but $\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{3} = \sqrt{6}$ is irrational).

workedExamples.prompt: Show that 0.3333... = 0.bar(3) can be expressed in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q != 0.
steps: Step 2: Since only 1 digit repeats, multiply both sides by 10: 10x = 3.3333... (Equation 2).
Step 3: Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 2: 10x - x = (3.3333...) - (0.3333...).

practice.prompt: Which of the following numbers is IRRATIONAL?
hints: 7 is a prime number, so sqrt(7) cannot be written as p/q.
practice.feedback: sqrt(7) is irrational because 7 is not a perfect square. sqrt(4)=2 and sqrt(9/4)=1.5 are rational.

takeaways: Rational decimals either terminate or recur infinitely.
Non-terminating and non-recurring decimals are irrational.
The square root of any non-square natural number is irrational.
